A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Stationary MMD Points and contain readable main sections, seven figures, Table 1, and Appendices A–C. Layout changes and figure renumbering do not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original numerical integration and MMD benchmarks on Gaussian mixtures, House8L, and Elevators, together with stationarity checks and kernel analyses.

after.justification: v3 reports these original benchmarks and analyses, including higher-dimensional Gaussian-mixture results in Table 1.

M1.justification: The stationary-point construction and deterministic and noisy MMD particle updates in equations (7)–(8) are unchanged. Added discussion of subsampling does not introduce an implemented method component.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same Gaussian-mixture integration tasks, including dimensions 2, 10, and 50, and the House8L and Elevators evaluations. No dataset or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark plots retain IID, kernel herding, kernel thinning, and support points. Appendix C.2 retains the same centered-versus-uncentered KT comparisons.

E3.justification: Reported kernels, step sizes, noise schedules, iteration budgets, and candidate-pool procedures are retained. The new n=100 statement in Figure 4 documents an existing check rather than reporting a protocol revision.

E4.justification: The exact-integration and noise-condition checks, Matérn kernel ablation, and KT centering and oversampling analyses are unchanged. Moving two checks into the main text does not add analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report 20 independent runs with different seeds and 25%–75% quantile bands for the main benchmark plots. Table 1 retains the same ± reporting.

E6.justification: The plotted results and all Table 1 values match. Reported convergence slopes of −1.39 for integration error and −1.35 for MMD, as well as runtime comparisons, are unchanged.

T1.justification: Assumptions 1–5, the exactness and super-convergence results, finite-particle bounds, and Appendix B proofs retain their mathematical content. Repaired lemma references and the added seminorm clarification do not change the arguments.

C1.justification: The core claims remain super-convergence of stationary MMD points and their computation through noisy MMD descent with a finite-particle convergence guarantee. The introduction now identifies the existing noisy scheme more precisely.

C2.justification: New Remark 3.6 explains why non-uniqueness does not invalidate the integration guarantees. Section 4 adds qualifications about variance from subsampling and the computational cost of selecting noise levels through empirical checks.

D1.justification: Figure 4 newly specifies n=100 for the empirical verification of Assumption 5. The remaining implementation details and the code-access link are unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds six references and a short paragraph connecting MMD constructions to sampling, compression, integration, and attention. Additions include Chizat et al. on MMD-flow convergence, Hazan et al. on graduated optimization, and Schröder and Mackey's Wildcat; the central positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Limited explanatory additions, corrected B.5/B.6 references, acknowledgments, and updated author information accompany a switch to numbered citations. The main section and appendix organization remains substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from single-column presentation to a two-column ICML layout, with revised typography, headers, and display sizing. The existing exact-integration and noise-condition plots move from Appendix C into the main text; the benchmark figure is renumbered from Figure 2 to Figure 3.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves clarity and reproducibility through practical qualifications, the noise-check particle count, and repaired lemma references. Bringing supporting checks into the main text improves accessibility, although a stale Section C pointer to Figure 4 remains. The theoretical and empirical substance is unchanged, so the gains are limited.
